messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: Using character strings as arguments
parts:
aes_string() is your friend. 

?aes_string()

On Sat, Oct 13, 2012 at 2:47 PM, Chris Brien <chris...@iinet.net.au> wrote:
I have the name of the x variable, xDay, stored as a character, x.num say, and the actual values of the variable are stored in a data frame, say pred.

I could call ggplot as follows:

plot <- ggplot(data = pred, aes(x = xDay, y = response))

However, I want to use x.num to specify the x variable. So I tried to set up the plot using

plot <- ggplot(data = pred, aes(x = x.num, y = response))

and

plot <- ggplot(data = pred, aes(x = as.name(x.num), y = response))

Neither works. Does anyone know how I can use x.num to supply the name of the x variable?

Cheers,

 Chris
